name: Bold
label: Revelation
lede: Four Westchester kids who were too young to get into CBGB made one album in Youth of Today's studio, lifted the cover idea from Run-D.M.C., and watched it outlive the band by decades.

eras.title: Too young for the door
eras.text: Katonah is forty miles north of the city, and Matt Warnke was 13 or 14 when he found hardcore through record shops, fanzines and friends' older siblings. He and his John Jay High School friends were playing CBGB matinees before most of them could legally walk in.

years.p: Matt Warnke on vocals and guitar, [[Tim Brooks|f8e01057-29f6-4be5-968e-4220d6a48ff3]] on bass, [[Drew Thomas|ebc66701-0d59-49c9-ae21-4937edb96a6a]] on drums. Warnke is under 16, so his first trips to CBGB mean standing outside.
years.xp: The record that hit Warnke hardest was [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]]'s Victim in Pain.

years.h: Crippled Youth's Join the Fight 7" · New Beginning Records
years.p: Crippled Youth recorded their debut in December 1985. Mike Trouchon's California label, New Beginning, put it out in 1986.
years.xp: The record got a feature in Maximum Rock'N'Roll. The first sleeves went out with the layout ruler accidentally left in under the back-cover photo. It's the earliest material Revelation later gathered on The Search.

years.h: Crippled Youth's first CBGB matinee, with [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]] and [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]]
years.p: Matt Warnke's first official show at the Bowery club, on a bill with [[Rest In Pieces|3cb8bd68-6c42-4dea-b0c6-f33c66cc790b]], Warzone and Youth of Today. John Zuluaga, known as Zulu, joins on guitar and Warnke moves to vocals only.
years.xp:
Matt Warnke had been going to CBGB since 1985, but under 16 that mostly meant hanging around outside. The June 1986 matinee was his first time through the door officially, and he was on stage.

The same van rides into the city delivered the other big shock of that year: hearing the [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]] demo, which Warnke remembers as a cultural shift.

eras.title: Speak Out
eras.text: By the time the kids had a full-length in them they'd dropped the name Crippled Youth for Bold, and a California label was lined up to put the album out. Then Jordan Cooper made his case, and it became Revelation No. 9.

q: At the time, I was definitely not thinking about longevity.
years.p: Bold's debut album was meant for Wishing Well Records in Orange County until Jordan Cooper talked the band into giving it to Revelation instead.
years.xp:
Wishing Well was Pat Dubar and Pat Longrie's label. Bold recorded at Electric Reels with Dan Nichols producing, the studio where Youth of Today had cut Break Down the Walls; the working title was Reach Out. The look came from outside hardcore: Matt Warnke pointed to Run-D.M.C.'s Raising Hell and Stetsasonic's On Fire for the tinted photos and block logo, and Van Halen's first album for the quadrant layout.

About ten years later Speak Out got a second life, as a straight edge revival in Ohio spread outward and new kids went looking for the originals. Guitarist John Zuluaga admits nobody in the band was thinking that far ahead.

years.h: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988
yt: Side By Side, Gorilla Biscuits and Bold live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, January 15, 1988

eras.title: Three songs and a second album nobody heard yet
eras.text: With Tom Capone adding a second guitar, Bold got heavier and more careful. They cut one more 7" and a second record in 1989, then scattered into the bands that pushed New York hardcore somewhere new.

years.p: Three songs, and the first record with [[Tom Capone|88c3e80c-41b6-48c9-985c-26ad5d026abd]] on second guitar. The colored vinyl was supposed to be maroon to match the sleeve, but the plant couldn't mix it right and it came out pink.
Drew Thomas helps start [[Into Another|c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8]] in 1990. Tom Capone goes on to [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]], and later Handsome and Instruction.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates Bold's run to 1993, but no later shows or records are documented.

years.h: Bold's Looking Back comes out, two years after the band's last session
years.p: Bold cut their final recordings by February 1989. Revelation released them as Looking Back in 1991.
years.xp: Revelation later reissued Looking Back as a 12" with two bonus tracks.

eras.title: The Bold that wasn't
eras.text: Matt Warnke got back on stage with a new band that played some old Bold songs and had no name of its own. A Connecticut flyer billed them as Bold, and not everyone was happy about it.

q: This isn't BOLD, but we're going to do some of those songs.
years.h: Billed as Bold at the New Milford Teen Center
years.p: Matt Warnke's new band with Eddie McNamara, Chris Daley and Matt Martin had already played the Wetlands and CBGB. Booked in Connecticut, they were billed as Bold, and people took it for a reunion.
years.xp:
The band had no settled name and was mixing Bold songs into a new, post-hardcore set. Eddie McNamara told the crowd so from the stage.

The real reunion, with the Speak Out core, was still nine years away.

eras.title: The real reunion
eras.text: Revelation's retrospective brought Bold back together, with an old friend from Youth of Today and Judge on second guitar. By the label's 25th birthday they were a fixture of its anniversary bills on both coasts.

years.p: Sixty-six minutes: Looking Back, Speak Out, compilation tracks, two unreleased songs and the Crippled Youth 7", running backwards in time from the last session to the first.
Matt Warnke, Tom Capone and Tim Brooks, with Vinny Panza on drums and [[John Porcelly|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]] sitting in on second guitar.

years.h: Matt Warnke and John Porcelly leave the Bold reunion
years.p: The singer and the guest guitarist step away, which Wikipedia says effectively ends Bold again.

years.h: Bold at Revelation 25, the Glasshouse in Pomona
years.p: Bold play the West Coast leg of Revelation Records' 25th anniversary.

years.h: Bold at Revelation 25, Irving Plaza in New York
years.p: Bold play the New York leg of Revelation's 25th anniversary, back in the city whose matinees they grew up in.

eras.title: Thirty-five and embossed
eras.text: Revelation gave Speak Out the full 35th-anniversary treatment, and Bold kept playing to people who weren't born when it came out.

years.p: Revelation puts out a Speak Out remaster in an embossed gatefold with a 40-page booklet designed by John Scharbach, plus color variants and a cassette.

years.h: Bold's West Coast run, with John Porcelly back
years.p: Bold play a run of California shows with [[John Porcelly|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]] in the second guitar spot again.

Bold and Youth of Today play the Meadows in Brooklyn, the Lithuanian Music Hall in Philadelphia and Amityville Music Hall, with Swedish Revelation band Speedway opening. The two bands had shared a CBGB bill in June 1986.
A $30 bill at Conduit, Bold opening for the reunited New York post-hardcore band.
